s1.syndrome_frame: obstructive uropathy with renal impairment in a newborn
key_facts: 36 weeks' gestation at referral
Prenatal ultrasound showed bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis
Prenatal ultrasound showed a markedly dilated fetal bladder
Left perirenal fluid collection measured 64 × 34 mm
Left perirenal fluid collection contained multiple light bands, flocculent echoes, and slightly echogenic material
Oligohydramnios present
Emergency cesarean delivery
Male infant with weight 2530 g
Apgar scores of 8, 8, and 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
Stable vital signs
Normal physical examination
Elevated serum creatinine at 156.1 µmol/L
Postnatal MRI showed mixed long and short T1 and T2 signals with internal light bands in the left perirenal collection
Magnetic resonance urography revealed bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention

shortlist.label: Posterior urethral valves
shortlist.why_kept: Obstructive uropathy with renal impairment, consistent with prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, and postnatal MRI showing bladder wall irregularity and thickening

shortlist.label: Prune belly syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by renal impairment, urinary tract anomalies, and abdominal muscle deficiency, which aligns with the prenatal and postnatal findings of renal enlargement, hydronephrosis, and bladder abnormalities

shortlist.label: Urethral atresia
shortlist.why_kept: Obstructive uropathy with renal impairment, consistent with prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, and postnatal MRI showing bladder wall irregularity and thickening

shortlist.label: Congenital ureteropelvic junction obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Causes hydronephrosis and renal impairment, consistent with prenatal ultrasound findings and postnatal MRI results

shortlist.label: Multicystic dysplastic kidney
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by renal cysts and dysplasia, which may be associated with obstructive uropathy and renal impairment, consistent with prenatal and postnatal imaging findings

raw.rationale: The prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, a markedly dilated fetal bladder, and oligohydramnios, along with the postnatal MRI and magnetic resonance urography results showing bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention, are consistent with the obstructive uropathy caused by posterior urethral valves.

rejected.label: Prune belly syndrome
rejected.why: While prune belly syndrome can cause renal anomalies and urinary tract issues, it typically involves abdominal muscle deficiency and undescended testes, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Urethral atresia
rejected.why: Urethral atresia would likely cause more severe oligohydramnios and potentially other anomalies, which are not described in the case.

rejected.label: Congenital ureteropelvic junction obstruction
rejected.why: This condition typically causes unilateral hydronephrosis, whereas the case describes bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis.

rejected.label: Multicystic dysplastic kidney
rejected.why: This condition would not explain the bilateral ureteral dilation, bladder wall irregularity, and urinary retention observed in the case.
